little.twist: A car is hidden round the bend: listen for it. And no glow shows you when it is safe.
little.can_now: stop at the kerb, look {look_order} and listen, and wait for a big gap before crossing with a grown-up

steps.say: This is the practice street. Real cars drive here at real speeds, but this is practice. Gus the grown-up buddy will cross with you.
Near roads, hold a grown-up's hand. Hold Gus's hand.
steps.done: Holding hands: safe and together.

steps.say: Walk to the kerb, the edge of the pavement, and stop just before it.
steps.done: Stop! You stopped at the kerb.

steps.say: Look all around: {look_order}. The nearest cars come from the {first_side}.
steps.done: You looked {look_order}. Looking is how you stay safe.

steps.say: Shh... listen. Can you hear a car coming round the bend?

choices.why: Listen again: you can hear an engine. Wait until it has gone.

steps.done: You listened. Your ears help your eyes.

steps.say: Now listen. Cars make a noise. What do you do while you listen?

choices.why: Never run across. Stand still at the kerb and listen.

steps.done: Standing still and listening: well done.

steps.say: Wait until there is a big gap and no car is coming. Then cross with Gus.
steps.miss: Wait! A car is coming. The car stops. Step back and wait for a big gap.
steps.done: You waited for a big gap. Walk straight across, keep looking and listening.

steps.say: Now you judge the gap: wait until no car is coming, then cross with Gus.
steps.miss: Wait! A car is coming. The car stops. Step back and wait for a big gap.
steps.done: You judged the gap by yourself. Walk straight across, keep looking and listening.

steps.say: Across! Walk, don't run, and keep looking and listening while you cross.
Oh! A ball rolls into the road. What do you do?

choices.text: Stay on the pavement and ask a grown-up

choices.why: Never run into the road after a ball. A grown-up can get it safely.

steps.done: Stay on the pavement. A grown-up gets the ball.

steps.say: Now the car. It is parked at the kerb with its back door open. Let's practise getting in safely.
Where do children sit in a car?

choices.text: In the back, in a booster seat

choices.why: Children are safest in the back seat, in a child seat or a booster seat.

steps.done: In the back, in your booster seat.

steps.say: Climb in and sit in the booster seat.
steps.done: Sitting back in the booster seat.

steps.say: Pull the belt across you and push it into the buckle.
steps.done: Click! The belt is on.

steps.say: Where does the belt go?

choices.text: Over the shoulder, low on the hips

choices.why: Not on the neck: the belt goes over the middle of your shoulder.
Never under the arm. Over the shoulder and across the chest.

steps.done: Over the shoulder, low across the hips. A booster seat makes it fit.

steps.say: You did it! Stop at the kerb, look and listen, wait for a big gap, cross with a grown-up, and belt up in the back.

check.say: You want to cross the road. Where do you stop?
At the kerb, what do you do?

choices.text: When there is a big gap

check.say: Where do you sit in a car?

name_it.title: Stop, look, listen, think
lines: Hold a grown-up's hand near roads.
Wait for a big gap, then walk straight across.
In the car: the back seat, a booster seat, belt on.
name_it.source: The road safety authorities' advice (the WHO, the UK's Green Cross Code, the US NHTSA)

little.try_real: With a grown-up, on a quiet street: stop at the kerb together, look {look_order} and listen. Show your grown-up how you wait for a big gap. In the car, show them how your belt fits.

sources.fact: The Green Cross Code: think, stop at the kerb, look all around and listen, wait until it is safe, look and listen as you cross; young children cross with a grown-up.
sources.source: The Highway Code (UK), rules for pedestrians, Rule 7 and Rules 4-6

sources.fact: Children ride in the back seat, in a car seat or a booster seat until the adult belt fits: the shoulder belt across the shoulder and chest, not the neck; the lap belt low on the hips and upper thighs, not the stomach.
sources.source: NHTSA, car seats and booster seats

sources.fact: Road traffic injuries are among the biggest dangers to children and young people worldwide; children walking near traffic are among the most at risk.
sources.source: WHO, road traffic injuries fact sheet

sources.fact: Practising street crossing in virtual reality improved children's crossing behaviour after several short sessions.
sources.source: Schwebel et al., randomized trials of VR pedestrian training

middle.skill: Crossing alone, at night and on a bike
middle.twist: The green man starts to flash just as you get there, and at night a car comes fast.
middle.can_now: cross at a button crossing on the green man, step out from parked cars only to their edge, be seen at night, and fit a bike helmet

steps.say: The practice street again: you cross alone today. A van is parked here. Drivers can't see you behind it, and you can't see them.
Go to the edge of the van, where you can see and be seen. Stop there: never step into the road to look.
steps.done: At the edge, like a kerb.

steps.say: Look {look_order}. The nearest cars come from the {first_side}.
steps.done: You looked round the van both ways.

safe_mistake.wrong: stepping out from behind a parked van while a car comes
safe_mistake.why: Behind a parked van the drivers can't see you, and a car needs time to stop: it couldn't stop in time.
safe_mistake.right: Wait at the van's edge, where drivers can see you, until there is a big gap.

steps.say: Wait for a big gap, then walk straight across.
steps.miss: Wait! A car is coming. Stay at the edge of the van until there is a big gap.
steps.done: A big gap: you crossed. Keep looking and listening.

steps.say: Now a button crossing. The button makes the traffic lights stop the cars for you.
Press the button.
steps.done: WAIT lights up. Wait for the green man.

steps.say: The red man shows. What does it mean?

choices.why: The red man means don't cross. Wait for the green man.

steps.done: Wait for the green man.

safe_mistake.wrong: starting to cross before the green man
safe_mistake.why: Before the green man the cars still have their green light: they keep going, and a car can't stop in a moment.
safe_mistake.right: Wait for the green man, and check the cars have stopped.

steps.say: When the green man shows, check the cars have stopped, then cross. If it flashes before you start, wait for the next one.
steps.miss: Not yet: wait for the green man, and for the cars to stop.
steps.done: The green man, the cars stopped: you crossed.

safe_mistake.wrong: starting to cross before the green man
safe_mistake.why: Before the green man the cars still have their green light: they keep going, and a car can't stop in a moment.
safe_mistake.right: Wait for the green man, and check the cars have stopped.

steps.say: When the green man shows, check the cars have stopped, then cross. If it flashes before you start, wait for the next one.
steps.miss: Not yet: wait for the green man, and for the cars to stop.
steps.done: The green man, the cars stopped: you crossed.

steps.say: Now it is getting dark. In the dark, drivers find it hard to see people walking.
What helps drivers see you at night?

choices.text: Light clothes and something that shines

choices.why: Dark clothes are hard to see at night. Wear something light, and something that shines in car lights.

steps.done: Light colours, and something that shines in the headlights.

steps.say: Put on the shiny band. It glows when car lights shine on it.
steps.done: It shines! Drivers see you from far away.

steps.say: Switch on the torch.
steps.done: A light helps you see, and be seen.

safe_mistake.wrong: stepping out when headlights are coming
safe_mistake.why: In the dark it is hard to tell how fast a car is coming, and drivers see you later.
safe_mistake.right: Wait for a big gap, with no headlights coming.

steps.say: Cross in the dark: stop, look {look_order}, listen, wait for a big gap. Car lights can be far away and still come fast.
steps.miss: Wait! Headlights are coming. Wait for a big gap.
steps.done: You judged the gap in the dark.

steps.say: Daylight again. Pip-pop is going for a bike ride. Let's check her helmet fits.
Which helmet fits?

choices.why: Tipped back, it can't protect the forehead. It sits level, two fingers above the eyebrows.

steps.done: Level on the head.

steps.say: Put two fingers above Pip-pop's eyebrows: the helmet sits just there.
steps.done: Two fingers: just right.

steps.say: Slide the straps so they make a V under each ear.
steps.done: A V under each ear.

steps.say: Buckle it under the chin.
steps.done: Click!

steps.say: One finger should fit under the chin strap, no more.
steps.done: Snug, not tight. Pip-pop is ready to ride.

steps.say: Well done! The edge of a parked car, the green man, being seen at night, and a helmet that fits.

check.say: A van is parked. Where do you look from?
The green man is flashing and you haven't started. What do you do?
At night, what helps drivers see you?

choices.text: Light clothes and a shiny band

check.say: How far above the eyebrows does a helmet sit?

name_it.title: Cross safely, be seen
lines: Use a crossing when there is one: wait for the green man and check the cars have stopped.
Parked cars: stop at their edge, look and listen.
At night: light clothes, something that shines, a light.
Bike helmet: level, two fingers above the eyebrows, a V under each ear, one finger under the strap.
name_it.source: The UK Highway Code's rules for pedestrians and the US NHTSA's helmet fit advice

middle.try_real: With a grown-up, walk to a button crossing and show them every step. At home, fit your bike helmet in front of a mirror: two fingers, a V, one finger.

sources.fact: Parked vehicles: use the outside edge of the vehicles as if it were the kerb; stop there and make sure you can see all around and that the traffic can see you.
At a button (pelican or puffin) crossing: press the button, wait for the green figure, check the traffic has stopped, then cross with care; do not start to cross if the green figure is flashing.
Help others see you: wear something light-coloured, bright or fluorescent in daylight, and reflective materials in the dark.
A helmet fits when it sits level, about two fingers above the eyebrows, the side straps form a V under the ears, and the buckled chin strap lets about one finger fit under it.
Being visible (light, bright and reflective clothing) helps pedestrians at night.
sources.source: WHO, pedestrian safety: a road safety manual

big.twist: A ball rolls into the road ahead: brake in time, and expect a child after it.
big.can_now: explain the rules of the road from the driver's seat: belts, the traffic lights, giving way to people crossing, the speed limit and never a phone

steps.say: The driver's seat of a practice car: it stands still on rollers, so nothing can go wrong. Drivers follow rules that keep everyone safe. Let's see them.
First, the seat belt: pull it across and click it in.
steps.done: Click. Belt on, every trip.

steps.say: Who wears a seat belt in a car?

choices.why: Everyone wears one, in the front and the back, on every trip, even short ones.

steps.done: Everyone, every seat, every trip.

steps.say: The light ahead turns red. What does the driver do?

choices.why: Red means stop and wait behind the line, every time.

steps.done: Stop at the line.

steps.say: Press and hold the brake pedal (in VR: the trigger) until the car stops.
steps.done: Stopped at the red light.

steps.say: People cross on their green man while your light is red. Wait for them: they have the right of way.
What does an amber light mean?

choices.text: Stop, unless it isn't safe to stop

choices.why: Amber means stop at the line, unless you are so close that stopping would not be safe.

steps.done: Amber: stop if you safely can.

steps.say: Now the light is green. What does green mean?

choices.text: Go, if the way is clear

choices.why: Green means you may go, but only if the way is clear: look for people still crossing.

steps.done: Go only when the way is clear.

steps.say: Press the accelerator gently. Keep the needle at the limit on the sign, {speed_limit} {speed_unit}, or below, for 4 seconds.
steps.done: Steady, at the limit. Near schools and homes, slow is safe.

steps.say: A ball rolls into the road ahead! What does the driver do?

choices.text: Brake: a child may run after it

choices.why: Where there is a ball, a child may follow. Brake and be ready to stop.

steps.done: Expect a child after a ball.

steps.say: Brake!
steps.done: You stopped in time.

steps.say: The phone buzzes while you are driving. What do you do?

choices.text: Leave it: never a phone while driving

choices.why: A phone takes your eyes and your mind off the road. Leave it; stop safely first if you must.

steps.done: Eyes on the road. The phone can wait.

steps.say: A car at 20 mph (about 30 km/h) needs about 12 metres to stop. At 30 mph (about 50 km/h)?

choices.text: About 23 metres: nearly twice as far

choices.why: Faster needs much more room: about 23 metres at 30 mph. That is why limits near schools are low.

steps.done: Faster needs much more room to stop.

steps.say: A cyclist is ahead. How much room do you give when you pass?

choices.why: Give cyclists plenty of room, at least 1.5 metres in town, and pass slowly.

steps.done: Plenty of room, and slowly.

steps.say: Someone waits at a zebra crossing. What do you do?

choices.why: Give way to people waiting at a zebra crossing: slow down and stop for them.

steps.done: People first at a crossing.

steps.say: You know the rules of the road: belts on, stop at red, give way to people, keep to the limit, and never a phone. As a walker, you now know what drivers see.

name_it.title: The rules of the road
lines: Everyone belted, every seat, every trip.
Red: stop. Amber: stop if you safely can. Green: go if the way is clear.
Keep to the limit: faster needs much more room to stop.
name_it.source: The UK Highway Code (rules for drivers) and the WHO's road safety facts

big.try_real: On your next car trip, be the safety helper: check everyone's belt before the car moves, and spot the traffic lights and the crossings with your grown-up.

sources.fact: Traffic lights: red means stop and wait behind the stop line; amber means stop unless you have crossed the line or are so close that pulling up might cause a collision; green means you may go on if the way is clear, giving way to pedestrians who are crossing.
Typical stopping distances: about 12 metres at 20 mph and about 23 metres at 30 mph.
It is illegal to hold a phone while driving; give cyclists at least 1.5 metres when overtaking at speeds up to 30 mph; give way to pedestrians waiting at a zebra crossing.
Seat belts cut the risk of a fatal injury for drivers and front-seat passengers by 45-50%, and the risk of serious injury for rear-seat passengers by about 25%; lower speeds save lives.
sources.source: WHO, road traffic injuries fact sheet
